prompt:
# Marketplace trust boundary

CRITICAL VISUAL RULE: tell the story without typography or interface graphics. All packages, gates, clothing, walls, and screens must be blank. Do not draw the GitHub logo, Octocat/Invertocat silhouette, wordmark, letters, numbers, code, charts, interface controls, badges, or labeled icons.

Create premium animated 16:9 GitHub key art, composed safely inside a 3:2 generation canvas. Render a polished 2.5D animated-film still with cel-shaded characters, GitHub dark-mode depth, contribution-grid texture, repository-like packages, crisp Octicon-inspired geometry, and restrained depth. Use approximately 80% near-black or off-white, 10% neutral gray, 5% GitHub green, and 5% Copilot purple.

Show an animated developer escorting abstract extension packages toward a protected developer environment. Move the packages through five distinct, unlabeled checkpoints represented only by identity, lock, pulse, lifeline, and rollback-inspired geometry; one package is visibly held outside the boundary while approved packages pass. The visual POV is that convenience changes the trust boundary and onboarding must remain reversible.

Place the scene on the right and preserve the left 42% for slide copy. No logos, mascots, generic app-store shelf, words, letters, real product interface, screenshots, interface panels, or watermarks.
